## b58ebf4ada2f

**Finding: reproduced three-demo teaching ambiguity — all diagonal 8s may appear
to become 4.**

The authority has two diagonal branches: some diagonal 8s become 4 while others
remain 8, according to separator-diamond geometry. The generator guarantees an
aligned-stay branch and a diagonal-change branch, but diagonal-stay examples are
rare enough that three consecutive generated demonstrations can omit them.

An exact ordinary sequence is `difficulty="easy"`, `seed=1`, sample indices
`[1,2,3,4]`. All four grids pass the target `self_check`. In samples 1–3 no
diagonal 8 remains 8, so the plausible rival “aligned 8s stay 8; every diagonal
8 becomes 4” matches every canonical Racket output. In held-out sample 4, the
rival changes two lawful preserved cells to 4:

- `(11,13)`: authority 8, rival 4
- `(12,12)`: authority 8, rival 4

The exact four input grids and all Racket/rival outputs are retained in
`checks/audit/b58ebf4ada2f/inputs.json` and
`checks/audit/b58ebf4ada2f/evidence.json`, bound to generator SHA-256
`f867a532620f0ec0293dd9d84a5760abc1fa405b8b01d081db27e5d0de657920`.
A supplementary 1,000-draw-per-band local census observed a diagonal-stay branch
in only 2.4% of easy draws, 3.7% of default/medium draws, and 6.2% of hard draws;
the saved lesson itself is checked against canonical Racket outputs rather than
that local mirror.

**Suggested maintainer action.** Use a deterministic short schedule that places at
least one diagonal-stay case in every three-demo window, then register and test the
`all_diagonal_to_four` rival. No patch is included because this was an audit-only
target.
